name: torchquad
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set name = "torchquad" %}
{% set org = "esa" %}
{% set version = "0.6.0" %}
{% set sha256 = "92f87b771e9a1e26ec5f25c55b37ea6eb8a477fc0c0aa6873dd687e6a245557b" %}

package:
  name: {{ name|lower }}
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/{{ org }}/{{ name }}/archive/refs/tags/v{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: {{ sha256 }}

build:
  noarch: python
  number: 0
  script: {{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv

requirements:
  host:
    - python {{ python_min }}
    - pip
    - setuptools >=77.0.3
  run:
    - python >={{ python_min }}
    - loguru >=0.5.3
    - autoray >=0.5.0
    - numpy >=1.21.3
    - scipy >=1.7.2

test:
  imports:
    - torchquad
  commands:
    - pip check
    # Sobol imports scipy.stats.qmc lazily, inside the sampler, so a scipy floor
    # that is too low passes the import test above and only fails once a user
    # reaches for quasi-Monte Carlo.
    - 'python -c "import numpy; from torchquad import Sobol; assert Sobol(''numpy'', seed=0).uniform([16, 2], numpy.float64).shape == (16, 2)"'
  requires:
    - pip
    - python {{ python_min }}

about:
  home: https://github.com/esa/torchquad/
  license: GPL-3.0-only
  license_family: GPL3
  license_file: LICENSE
  summary: torchquad provides torch-based numerical integration methods.
  description: |
    This project allows utilizing GPUs for efficient numerical 
    integration with PyTorch. It  is designed for the machine learning 
    community and research groups focusing on topics requiring high-dimensional 
    integration. By using PyTorch backpropagation through the integrals is possible.
  doc_url: https://torchquad.readthedocs.io/en/main/
  dev_url: https://github.com/esa/torchquad/

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - gomezzz
